A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Uni-DAD research and include readable main text and supplementary material. Equations, tables, figures, and relocated sections can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original FSIG experiments, component ablations, computational measurements, and three-subject personalization experiments, including supplementary Table 7.

after.justification: V2 retains the original FSIG experiments and reports personalization results across 30 DreamBooth subjects, additional comparisons, and new sensitivity and diversity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 revises the stated GAN objectives from hinge losses to sigmoid-based binary cross-entropy in Equations 8–9. V1 already selected BCE in Table 5, so this corrects the method specification without establishing changed implementation or retraining. The architecture, dual-domain DMD, training loop, and personalization conditioning are retained.

E1.justification: FSIG, personalization, and Starry Night style transfer already appear in v1. V2 Figure 8 adds explicit personalization scenarios requiring property changes, including purple and cube-shaped teapots, beyond the previously illustrated recontextualization and accessorization cases. The larger DreamBooth subject sample is assessed under E3.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds FT-DMD2 and DMD2-PSO on SDv1.5 to the personalization comparison, materially strengthening tests against two-stage pipelines and PSO under matching backbone and sampling budgets. DreamBooth becomes FT, DMD2-DreamBooth becomes DMD2-FT, and the existing PSO becomes Turbo-PSO; these are retained comparators. FSIG comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Personalization evaluation expands from three selected DreamBooth subjects to all 30 and adds Intra-LPIPS and Inter-LPIPS alongside identity and text-alignment metrics. V2 also introduces a groupwise weighting-factor sweep. The 25 prompts × 4 generation seeds per subject, principal training settings, and existing FSIG evaluation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds personalization sensitivity analysis for the dual-domain weight, with qualitative examples and separate live-subject/object CLIP-I results, plus within-prompt and across-prompt diversity comparisons in Figure 10. These substantially extend diagnostic evidence for personalization. Existing FSIG component, checkpoint, shot-count, NFE, and GAN-loss ablations are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: V2 Table 3 introduces ± reporting for personalization diversity scores, absent from v1; Uni-DAD Intra-LPIPS is 0.51±0.09. The statistic represented by ± and its aggregation unit are unspecified. Four generation seeds per prompt were already reported in v1, and additional independent training runs are not established.

E6.justification: V1 Table 7's individual and three-subject personalization scores are replaced by 30-subject results in v2 Table 3, with additional baseline and diversity entries. Uni-DAD's DINO/CLIP-I/CLIP-T averages change from 0.631/0.771/0.271 to 0.47/0.73/0.29 under different subject coverage, not a directly comparable performance change. New sensitivity findings are reported; existing FSIG table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 formally defines sigmoid discriminator outputs and replaces the hinge expressions in Equations 8–9 with logarithmic BCE objectives, resolving their mismatch with v1's selected loss. This is a mathematical specification correction. The DMD derivation, weighting equations, and remaining formal content are unchanged; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion now explicitly emphasize both FSIG and personalization across diffusion backbones. Claims of higher quality and outperforming two-stage pipelines are qualified to better or comparable quality and often outperforming. The central single-stage unification and component contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explains the personalization tradeoff between FT-DMD2's stronger identity scores and substantially lower diversity, and acknowledges reduced diversity relative to DreamBooth. It also qualifies distant-domain FSIG superiority and the multi-head discriminator's advantage, while adding a proposed explanation for WGAN instability. Existing GAN-sensitivity and training-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-repository URL instead of v1's promise of future public release. Appendix 8.4 documents initialization of the added personalization FT-DMD2 baseline, and Appendix 8.6 explains selecting a=0.75 through visual inspection without subject-specific tuning. Most hardware, hyperparameters, and training details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 removes the separate Google Research DreamBooth repository reference while retaining the DreamBooth paper. The scientific reference set and positioning against Codi, PSO, and guidance-distillation approaches otherwise remain substantially unchanged. Moving and condensing personalization related work is primarily structural.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized around two benchmarks: personalization moves from a supplementary chapter into the main setup and results, while most FSIG ablations and Algorithm 1 move into the supplement. The abstract, contributions, discussion, conclusion, and appendix organization are extensively revised, and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds personalization comparison and diagnostic figures, expands the comparison grid with FT-DMD2, and replaces the three-subject table with a benchmark-wide quality/diversity display. Computational costs move into the main text, FSIG ablation tables move to the appendix, and supplementary image grids are rearranged. This is substantial display reorganization beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important validation gap: v1's personalization evidence covered only three subjects and lacked an Adapt-then-Distill comparator and diversity measurements. Full-benchmark evaluation, added controls, and sensitivity/diversity analyses provide substantially stronger evidence for the central quality–diversity tradeoff. Corrected GAN equations and more qualified claims improve consistency. Undefined ± statistics, incomplete details for DMD2-PSO, and removal of individual subject scores limit transparency but do not outweigh these gains.
